article.story: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. -- — KK Bransford scored 25 points to lead No. 10 UCLA to a 90-80 victory over Tennessee on Sunday night. The Bruins (6-0) got help from Elina Aarnisalo with 22 points, Donovyn Hunter had 12 and Timea Gardiner scored 11 off the bench. The Lady Vols (6-1) were led by Kaylene Smikle with 27 points and 10 rebounds. Fatmata Janneh scored 12 and Jada Eads had 10. UCLA established itself as a dominant force inside. The Bruins were effective on the boards with a 45-33 edge. Sienna Betts led the way with 12. Tennessee dared the defending national champs to keep up with their uptempo pace throughout. UCLA's advantage of 40-32 points in the paint had a lot to do with the outcome. Bransford had 17 points at halftime as UCLA owned a 48-41 lead. Smikle had 12 points to lead Tennessee, which actually outscored the Bruins, 21-18, in the second quarter. The big difference for UCLA was its command of the boards, 27-13. Sienna Betts led the way with six rebounds. After testing her new roster and revitalized offense on six mid-majors, this was Tennessee coach Kim Caldwell’s unveiling against a quality opponent. … The Lady Vols lost their entire roster after last season. It was rebuilt to fit Caldwell’s favorite attack — uptempo, many substitutions, general chaos. UCLA, though, knows a little bit about makeovers. Coming off the national championship, the Bruins lost six players to the WNBA. Those six accounted for 76.1 points per game, which equals 90.7% of last year’s production. Out of the 200 minutes the Bruins had played this season heading into the Tennessee game, they only trailed for 44 seconds. Up Next UCLA: The Bruins will play St. John’s Tuesday in the Basketball Hall of Fame Women's Showcase at Mohegan Sun Arena. Tennessee: The Lady Vols will play Florida Gulf Coast Friday in the Coconut Hoops tournament. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college basketball coverage here
